$comment: EXAMPLE manifest. Replace the entries with your own; the roots below are the defaults.
Paths are relative to THIS file's directory unless they start with ~ (home) or are absolute.
Skills under roots.own.skillsSubdir with no entry here default to class 'local'.
Skills installed by `npx skills` are discovered from roots.agentsLock and need no entry.
Classes: local | vendored | npm | git-repo | cli

example-vendored-subdir.note: The common case. The skill owns its own upstream directory, so the whole subtree under dirname(path) is the install set — no `installs` needed.

example-vendored-at-repo-root.note: The skill lives at the repo ROOT, so it is a SUBSET of that root — the repo also holds a README, a LICENSE and install scripts. `installs` is required here; without it the check would report the repo's own furniture as missing, and rather than guess it falls back to comparing SKILL.md alone and says so in the report.

example-fork.note: A DERIVATIVE, not a copy — deliberately rewritten, so diffing its content is meaningless. The question is whether upstream moved past syncedUpstreamVersion. `forkOmits` records that this fork inlines upstream's references/ rather than carrying them as files. Set it only AFTER verifying the content genuinely matches: it silences the warning, so setting it early buries the gap it exists to reveal.
example-fork.update: read upstream at the new version, port what applies, then bump syncedUpstreamVersion

example-npm-cli.note: The PACKAGE version and the SKILL version are often separate series, so compare skill-to-skill at the upstream repo. `tagPattern` pins the integrity check to the release tag for the INSTALLED version — comparing against HEAD flags every commit a maintainer makes between releases, which is a false alarm, not a finding.
example-npm-cli.warn: Some vendor CLIs execute on unrecognised flags rather than printing help. Probe with `<tool> help`, never `<tool> --help`.

example-vendor-cli.warn: Vendor CLIs that 'set up your coding agent' fan out across EVERY detected agent root by default (.claude, .agents, .config/opencode, .factory), installing where no copy existed. Scope the target unless all-agents is intended.

example-local.note: Authored here, no upstream. Checked only by the own-checkout git comparison. Note that absence of an entry defaults to this too — which means 'no upstream recorded' and 'no upstream exists' are currently indistinguishable.

marketplace.note: Marketplace plugins self-heal on their own schedule. Deliberately not checked here.
